business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Fast-Fashion Apparel and Footwear

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Federal State; focus Canton of Zug as proposed registered seat)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Roman-cantonal heritage with Swiss Code of Obligations as unifying instrument)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on Investment Promotion and Protection (signed 2009, in force 2011, replacing the 1986 BIT)
Switzerland–European Union Free Trade Agreement of 22 July 1972
EFTA Convention of 4 January 1960 (Switzerland as EFTA State)
Switzerland–China Double Taxation Agreement of 25 May 2013 (as amended by the 2018 amending protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Arts. 621-641a (Aktiengesellschaft); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of 10 October 1997 (AMLA, SR 955.0), Arts. 2a, 3, 6 and 9; Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411), Arts. 1-24; FINMA Circular 2011/01 on Anti-Money Laundering duties of financial intermediaries.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or Commercial Register Extract of the founding corporate shareholder and its parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or Companies House of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the foreign state is a contracting party; otherwise Swiss Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Swiss incorporation agent and the Swiss resident director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary of the jurisdiction where each founding shareholder is residing or registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of identity of all directors, shareholders and beneficial owners above 25%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office, state registry or notary of the document holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled certified copy or original for inspection at the Swiss notary's office

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening and sanctions checks must cover all directors, officers, shareholders and beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated List, and the Swiss SECO State Secretariat for Economic Affairs sanctions and persons list. Real-time screening is required; screening results are valid for no more than 72 hours before a financial transaction or notarial acceptance. Confirmed matches must be escalated through a four-eyes review by the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) and reported to the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS) as necessary.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (Zentrale Firmenindex) operated by the Federal Office of Justice, in conjunction with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name of an Aktiengesellschaft must be written in one of Switzerland's official languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh) and in Latin script. English may appear only as an auxiliary descriptive element, never as the dominant legal-form identifier. The suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' is mandatory and must be placed at the end of the name when a name in German is used.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended by one further term of 90 days upon written application made before expiry. If the Commercial Register Office of Zug rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection with the same office within 30 days of the rejection decision, providing arguments on trademark distinctiveness and absence of deception. If the office maintains its refusal, an appeal may be filed with the Cantonal Administrative Court of Zug (Verwaltungsgericht des Kantons Zug) within 20 days of the final administrative decision; further review may be sought before the Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland (Bundesgericht) on questions of law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only if it consists of a physical Swiss registered address in the Canton of Zug that can accept correspondence, permit inspection of corporate documents, and is backed by a written domiciliation agreement with a regulated service provider. A pure mailbox or post-office-box-only arrangement will not satisfy Swiss substance requirements for an Aktiengesellschaft.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of approximately 5-8% per annum for a low-risk fast-fashion e-commerce enterprise during the first year of operation. Unannounced physical on-site inspections are uncommon but can be triggered by the Commercial Register Office, cantonal tax authority, or financial intelligence suspicions regarding inadequate substance or suspicious cash flows.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register name clearance and reservation fee for one primary corporate name (Canton of Zug)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official tariff under Article 21 of the Commercial Register Fee Ordinance (SR 221.411)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial drafting, certification and sealing of the Articles of Association (Statuten) and related incorporation resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public licensed in the Canton of Zug
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for notarial acts for an AG with minimum share capital of CHF 100,000; fixed statutory notarial fee per article set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO piercing, PEP screening and OFAC/UN/SECO sanctions compliance package for 3 directors and 2 ultimate beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent compliance screening provider approved by Swiss counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat market benchmark per legal entity and per screened individual, including real-time sanctions API and four-eyes manual review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille or Swiss Consular Legalization of shareholder corporate documents, powers of attorney and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent competent authority of origin (e.g., Secretary of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs) and the Swiss Embassy or Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory official fee per document plus Swiss consular legalization fee where the origin state is not a Hague Apostille contracting party

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application fee for final commercial register entry including Official Swiss Trade Gazette (SHAB) publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug and Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt (SHAB)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registration tariff based on nominal share capital category and SHAB publication fee under the Commercial Register Fee Ordinance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement for a virtual physical office address in the Canton of Zug for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Zug market benchmark of CHF 100-150 per month for a compliant physical registered address and mail handling

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, SR 220), Arts. 620-763 (provisions on the stock corporation, Aktiengesellschaft). Key formation sections: Arts. 625-638 (incorporation procedure, reports, and payment of capital), Art. 640 (application for registration), Art. 643 (content of the registration application), Art. 716a (non-transferable board duties), Art. 698 (powers of the general meeting). The Ordinance on the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterverordnung, SR 221.411), Arts. 1-94, governs filing mechanics.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office (e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zürich); supervisory and appellate authority: Swiss Federal Commercial Register Authority (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt EHRA) in Bern, within the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Commercial Register Entry (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister, Form A), submitted together with the notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde) and the Articles of Association (Statuten), authenticated by a Swiss notary public.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital is CHF 100,000 (OR Art. 621); at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash before registration and must be at the board's free disposal (OR Art. 632), evidenced by a bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung) from a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank. Contributions in kind (Sacheinlagen) require a notarized contribution report (Sacheinlagebericht, OR Art. 628). No separate state escrow account is required; the deposit is held in a corporate formation account blocked until registration and released automatically upon entry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board Resolution of [Company] AG is adopted by unanimous written consent of the founders on the incorporation date. It resolves: (1) the subscribed share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000 each, is acknowledged, and the banking confirmation of CHF 50,000 paid in cash at the board's free disposal is accepted; (2) the registered office is fixed at [street, postal code, city, canton], Switzerland; (3) Mr./Ms. X is appointed Chair of the board, Mr./Ms. Y board member, and Mr./Ms. Z managing director with sole signature authority; (4) the notary and agent are mandated to file incorporation with the Commercial Register Office; all acts conforming to the Swiss Code of Obligations and Articles of Association are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Check and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via the electronic state portal 'e-register.ch' or written application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-reservation application stating the proposed company name, legal form, and domicile. The name must be linguistically distinctive, truthful, and not misleading (OR Art. 950); it must not conflict with existing trade names in the Swiss Central Business Name Index (ZEFIX). Provide the draft Articles of Association to demonstrate compliance with statutory content. Upon clearance, obtain a written name reservation valid for a limited period (typically 2-4 weeks depending on canton).
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and registered office canton
Copy of founders' passports or identity cards
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Power of attorney if the application is filed by a third-party agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name containing a distinctive element (e.g., a personal surname or a geographical identifier) or add a clarifying phrase describing the business purpose; re-submission is typically processed within 24 hours through the canton's Commercial Register Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public (Notariat / Étude notariale) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a notary in the canton of the registered office. The notary verifies founders' identities and legal capacity, reads the Articles of Association aloud, and records the founders' declaration of incorporation (Errichtung). The Deed must state the company name, domicile, corporate purpose, share capital, par value of shares, number and type of shares, and organization, as required by OR Art. 626. The notary authenticates signatures, attaches the Articles as an annex, and issues certified copies for the bank and Commercial Register filing. The deed triggers the start of the three-month registration filing window under OR Art. 640 para. 2.
required_dossiers: Name reservation confirmation from the Commercial Register Office
Final version of the Articles of Association (Statuten)
Passports or identity documents of all founders
Declaration of acceptance of office by the future board members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, execute a supplemental notarial deed (Nachtrag) to rectify omissions; any missing annexes are requested from the founders and attached before authentication. Re-execution of the deed is required only if the three-month filing window lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Swiss Corporate Formation Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank (e.g., UBS, Zürcher Kantonalbank, Raiffeisen) – AML/KYC compliance desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked formation account in the name of the company under formation (e.g., '[Company] AG in Gründung'). Present the notarized Deed of Incorporation, the Articles of Association, and the passport of the account signatories. Complete the bank's client onboarding forms, including the Swiss anti-money-laundering declarations under the AMLA (GwG) and the beneficial-owner self-declaration (Form CDB 20). Deposit the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 in cash. Obtain from the bank a written bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung) stating that the amount is credited to the company and is at the free disposal of the board of directors upon registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde) and certified copy of the Articles of Association
Valid passport or identity card of each signatory and beneficial owner
Beneficial ownership and politically-exposed-person declarations (Form CDB 20 / GwG forms)
Draft corporate resolution naming the authorized account representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to incomplete KYC or CDB documentation, promptly rectify the beneficial-ownership declarations and resubmit; if the bank confirmation contains errors, request a corrected Bankbestätigung from the bank's regulatory compliance unit before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt), legal section; filing via 'e-register.ch' or in person with the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration application within three months from the notarized deed (OR Art. 640). The filing package must include Form A (Anmeldung zur Eintragung), the notarized deed and Articles, the bank confirmation of paid-up capital, the declaration of acceptance by each board member, and specimen signatures of all authorized signatories. The registry examines the application for formal and substantive legality, including compliance with the minimum capital rules and corporate purpose. Upon approval, the registry records the company, assigns a registration number and the federal UID, and certifies the legal personality of the company.
required_dossiers: Application Form A (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister)
Notarized Deed of Incorporation and final Articles of Association
Bank confirmation of paid-up capital (Bankbestätigung)
Declaration of acceptance signed by each member of the board of directors
Specimen signatures of all persons with signing authority (Unterschriftenproben)
Declaration on the appointment of auditors (if statutory audit is required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an inquiry (Vorfrage), respond in writing within the specified deadline (generally 20 days). If the application is rejected, rectify the stated deficiencies and re-submit; an appeal against the registry's refusal may be lodged with the Federal Commercial Register Authority (EHRA) in Bern within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce and Post-Registration Tax and Social Security Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office, Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB), Federal Tax Authority (ESTV/FTA), and Cantonal Social Security Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the Commercial Register automatically transmits the entry for publication in the SHAB; publication occurs typically within 48 hours and includes the company name, domicile, purpose, share capital, and authorized signatories. After publication, register the company as an employer with the cantonal compensation office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) for old-age and survivors' insurance, take out mandatory accident insurance (SUVA or private insurer), and register for VAT with the Federal Tax Authority on Form S-087 if the projected annual worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000. Confirm the cantonal and municipal tax registration and the payment of federal, cantonal, and communal income taxes; apply for the UID confirmation and commercial register extract for the corporate bank account release.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract confirming registration (Handelsregisterauszug)
UID business identifier confirmation from the Central Business Name Index (ZEFIX)
VAT registration form S-087 for the Federal Tax Authority (ESTV)
AHV/social insurance employer registration form for the cantonal compensation office
SUVA or private accident insurance confirmation
Cantonal and municipal tax registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, contact the SHAB publication service with the registry file number. If the UID or VAT registration is held up, follow up with the Federal Tax Authority via the e-service portal and provide the commercial register confirmation; appeal or correction of registry data can be requested from the cantonal Commercial Register Office and, on appeal, from the EHRA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Office for Economic Affairs and Labour (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit, AWA) and the municipal business licensing office (Gewerbepolizei). For ISIC 4791 (electronic retailing of fast-fashion apparel), no industrial manufacturing or sectoral retail license is required; only a municipal business notification (Betriebsanmeldung) and zoning clearance for office and warehousing premises are mandatory.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no sector-specific operating license is prescribed for e-commerce apparel retail under Swiss federal law. A municipal business notification (Betriebsanmeldung) and a building/zoning conformity clearance (Bewilligung) for the registered office and warehouse address must nonetheless be obtained from the respective commune.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU/FOEN) and the Cantonal Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umwelt) of the registered office canton
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. E-commerce warehousing of apparel is not listed in Annex 2 of the Swiss EIA Ordinance (Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfungs-Verordnung, UVPV/OEIE); no full EIA or preliminary assessment is required. The operator must still comply with the Swiss Waste Ordinance (VVEA) for packaging, cardboard, and textile waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater is generated by e-commerce apparel retail; compliance with the Waters Protection Act (Gewässerschutzgesetz, GSchG) Art. 7 is limited to building surface runoff. VOC and chemical emission thresholds under the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (LRV) and the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ChemRRV) are not triggered for pure storage and repacking; if the operator engages in textile printing or chemical treatment, a prior authorization and emission declaration would become mandatory. Packaging waste must be separately collected and meet the recovery quotas of the Waste Ordinance (VVEA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required from the cantonal fire prevention authority (e.g., Schutz & Rettung Zürich or the cantonal insurance company Gebäudeversicherung) for commercial and warehouse use, including escape-route planning and fire extinguisher installation. A structural load inspection (Statiknachweis) certified by an engineer is required for storage racks exceeding 1.8 m in height. Occupational health and safety clearance must be obtained from the Cantonal Labour Inspectorate (Arbeitsinspektorat) under the Swiss Labour Act (ArG) and Ordinance 3 (ArGV 3), covering lighting, ventilation, rest areas, and ergonomic workstations. Accident prevention certification under EKAS/SUVA is needed for warehousing equipment; if working hours exceed the statutory thresholds of ArG Art. 9, a special work-time permit from the canton is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV/FTA), Eigerstrasse 65, CH-3003 Bern; online portal estv.admin.ch with eServices/SecurePortal for VAT registration and filings; UID register operated by the Federal Statistical Office at uid.admin.ch; company data accessible via Zefix (zefix.ch). Cantonal income tax is administered by the cantonal tax administration for the seat canton (e.g., Zug: Dienststelle Steuern, zg.ch).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Notarially execute articles of incorporation and register the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) in the Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregister); the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce publishes the entry. Step 2: The Federal Statistical Office automatically issues the Swiss Business Identification Number (UID, format CHE-123.456.789) upon commercial registration; no separate application is required. Step 3: Apply to the FTA for VAT registration via Form 716/eServices within 30 days after the VAT liability arises (worldwide turnover above CHF 100,000 or voluntary registration); the VAT number is the UID suffixed with MWST (CHE-123.456.789 MWST), being the statutory Swiss tax ID. Step 4: The FTA and cantonal tax administration open the corporate income tax file automatically from the commercial register notification; file annual federal and cantonal tax returns. Non-resident sellers without a commercial register entry must obtain a UID via the UID-A application to the competent cantonal administration and register for Swiss VAT through the FTA eServices before commencing taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation for the AG (collective capital company, minimum share capital CHF 100,000 under Art. 621 CO). The AG is taxed as a separate taxpayer on worldwide profits: federal corporate income tax at 8.5% (effective approximately 4.4% after gross-up) plus cantonal and communal profit tax (combined effective rates vary, e.g., roughly 11.9% in Zug) and cantonal capital tax. Swiss law applies a classical-like system with shareholder-level dividend relief (Teilsatzverfahren) and participation exemption; there is no pass-through eligibility and no territorial-exemption election; residence is governed by statutory seat and place of effective management. No tax-exempt zone applies to this entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no check-the-box or US-style entity classification election; tax classification follows legal form. Available elections: (1) Steuergruppe group taxation under the Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (TRAF) in force since 1 January 2020, permitting a qualifying parent to elect consolidated federal and cantonal profit/capital taxation of 100% owned Swiss subsidiaries; (2) VAT group election under Art. 12 VAT Act forming a fiscal unity for Swiss group companies; (3) small-business election under Art. 10 para. 2 VAT Act allowing taxable persons below the CHF 100,000 turnover threshold to elect either full VAT liability with input deduction or exemption; (4) election of VAT accounting basis (agreed consideration versus received consideration) subject to FTA approval; (5) foreign-currency accounting election for domestic financial statements under Art. 58 DBG; (6) notional interest deduction on surplus capital (capital contribution privilege, Art. 1 TRAF); and (7) cantonal incentive elections (patent box, R&D super-deduction, status privileges abolished as of 2020). No hybrid mismatch elections exist; Swiss ATAD-aligned rules and the Pillar Two qualified domestic minimum top-up tax (15%, Mindestbesteuerungsverordnung in force 1 January 2024) apply to in-scope MNE groups.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.territorial_scope: Worldwide income taxation for resident AG with unilateral/treaty foreign-tax relief, participation exemption and deemed capital interest; Swiss real estate and permanent establishments are subject to source cantonal taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_exempt_zone: None applicable; no Swiss free-port or special economic-zone regime alters the VAT or income tax classification of the CH_AG fast-fashion e-commerce entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_license_required_for_activity: None: e-commerce of apparel and footwear (ISIC 4791, NAICS 458110) is not a licensed activity in Switzerland; only a standard commercial register entry and UID are required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.payment_rails_tax_relevance: Klarna BNPL and Shopify Payments are immaterial to VAT classification: the Swiss VAT treatment of the underlying fashion supply governs; payment service provider fees are input-taxed domestic supplies subject to Swiss VAT at 8.1% where the provider is Swiss or applies reverse charge under Art. 45 VAT Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.other_statutory_notifications: The AG must notify the cantonal social security compensation fund (AHV) on commencement of business and report payroll for old-age and survivors insurance, as the e-commerce payroll creates Swiss social security obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.capital_tax: Cantonal capital tax on paid-up equity applies (rate varies by canton, typically 0.05% to 0.20% annually); no federal capital tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer/MWST, TVA, IVA) governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (SR 641.20), aligned with OECD International VAT/GST Guidelines and the destination principle.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 worldwide turnover per annum (Art. 10 para. 2 letter a VAT Act); reduced rates: 2.6% for basic necessities (food, books, medicines) and 3.7% for accommodation; a political proposal to raise the threshold to CHF 250,000 is pending and not yet enacted. Non-established remote sellers of goods or digital services to Swiss consumers may be taxable from the first franc of B2C digital supplies under Art. 7 para. 3 VAT Act, while the CHF 100,000 threshold applies to standard goods exports; B2B supplies to Swiss recipients are generally shifted to the recipient via reverse charge under Art. 45 and 51 VAT Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None: Switzerland has not introduced a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government-stamping, or statutory B2B e-invoicing clearance platform as of 2025. Electronic invoices (XML, EDI, Swiss QR-bill, eBill hub protocol) are legally valid under Art. 26 VAT Act and Art. 162 VAT Ordinance provided the statutory invoice content is present. The taxpayer must keep auditable electronic books and records for 10 years and grant FTA access to data stored domestically or abroad; no API pre-clearance to a governmental fiscal gateway is required. The Federal Council monitors the EU ViDA framework but has not enacted an equivalent Swiss mandate as of 2025.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of fast-fashion goods to foreign destinations qualifies for zero-rating (exempt with deduction) under Art. 23 para. 1 VAT Act where the AG proves physical dispatch abroad without undue delay, including e-commerce parcels via Swiss Post or courier with a customs export declaration; ancillary services directly related to exported goods and specified offshore services qualify under Art. 23 paras. 2–4 and Art. 21 para. 2 VAT Act. For C2B e-commerce exports, the exporter must retain destination-country customs clearance evidence; services supplied to recipients outside Switzerland are outside the Swiss VAT scope if not performed through a Swiss establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung) lodged electronically in the Federal Customs Administration e-dec system naming CH_AG as exporter and using the applicable export procedure code
Transport evidence: ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR international consignment note, or postal/courier export receipt with destination customs clearance tracking (CN23/CN22 for postal parcels)
Commercial or VAT invoice stating 'steuerfreie Exportlieferung (Art. 23 MWSTG)' and containing UID (MWST), foreign consignee address, goods description, quantity, and Incoterms

Proof of payment and foreign consideration: SWIFT/SEPA credit advice or payment-rail ledger confirmation; Swiss practice substitutes the formal Inward Remittance Certificate with auditable bank and ledger records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss VAT law imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export zero-rating; the 180-day figure is the conservative internal benchmark of the exporting group for assembling the export evidence file. The FTA audits export claims through book and document review under Art. 78 VAT Act; the assessment limitation period is generally 5 years after the tax period, extended to 10 years for intentional tax evasion. Missing or false export proof triggers retrospective assessment at 8.1% with default interest, and penalties under Art. 96 VAT Act of up to three times the evaded tax, or fines up to CHF 250,000 under Art. 100 VAT Act for negligent non-compliance; criminal fraud under Art. 146 Swiss Penal Code and loss of the right to deduct input VAT are further sanctions. The FTA may enforce joint and several liability against directors and group entities for e-commerce export schemes involving reimportation into Switzerland without applicable import VAT.

input_vat_recovery_mechanics.deduction_principle: The AG may deduct input VAT on domestic and import purchases that are used for taxable activities, including warehouse services, logistics, IT infrastructure, payment processing, marketing, and inventory imports to Switzerland; the deduction is effected in the periodic VAT return and by settling a credit balance, no separate refund procedure is required for resident exporters.
input_vat_recovery_mechanics.mixed_use_apportionment: VAT incurred for both business and private use must be apportioned by an approved method; the pro-rata deduction and the flat-rate method for partial use are available and require FTA acceptance.
input_vat_recovery_mechanics.point_of_tax: VAT becomes chargeable upon agreed consideration or upon invoice issue; imports are taxed upon customs clearance; the AG may elect to declare on a received-payment basis subject to FTA approval.
input_vat_recovery_mechanics.record_retention: All export and input VAT documents must be retained for 10 years in an auditable electronic format with FTA access rights, regardless of storage location.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB / Schweizerische Nationalbank) in conjunction with FINMA (Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority) for banking conduct; SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) and SIF (State Secretariat for International Finance) for sanctions and financial market policy. Foreign exchange policy is administered under the Federal Act on Currency and Means of Payment (WZG) and the SNB Act; no dedicated foreign exchange control law exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains a fully liberalised capital and current account regime. CHF is freely convertible; there are zero restrictions on foreign ownership, dividend repatriation, or cross-border payments for non-financial operating companies. No prior exchange control approval is required for inbound equity injections, intra-group loans, trade settlements, or profit remittance. Withholding tax of 35% applies to Swiss dividends (reducible under DTTs); this is a tax matter, not a currency control. For e-commerce flows denominated in EUR, USD and GBP, Swiss banks freely maintain multi-currency operating accounts; balances can be converted to CHF at market rates without notification to the SNB. The only administrative burden is the SNB monthly balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligation for transactions above CHF 10 million (cumulative) or as instructed by the SNB data collection framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, repatriation timeline, or minimum retention ratio on export receipts, including e-commerce proceeds from cross-border apparel sales. Exporters may hold proceeds indefinitely in foreign currency or convert freely. Reporting is limited to statistical disclosure: SNB Balance of Payments form (Zahlungsbilanzmeldung) for goods sold online abroad when total monthly inflows exceed the de minimis threshold; sales of goods to foreign consumers are declared as 'goods trade' (Warenhandel) and settled via ordinary banking channels without regulatory clearance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency EUR/USD/GBP/CHF) + segregated Capital Escrow sub-account for share capital reserve
Operational Account (primary CHF clearing via SIC) + e-commerce settlement account
Operational Account (regional cooperative) - useful for decentralised sub-ledgers
Payments concentration account for Swiss domestic e-commerce volumes and SEPA clearing

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Lombard Odier & Cie SA (private bank tier)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Escrow / treasury collateral account for high-value FX forwards and structured deposits

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as a treasury concentration venue; High as a payment-only gateway. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Currencycloud) are not licensed Swiss banks and cannot accept 'deposits' in the banking-law sense under Art. 1 Banking Act. Funds placed with these EMIs are not covered by the esisuisse deposit protection scheme (§37a Banking Act). For ISIC 4791 e-commerce treasury, an EMI may be used for high-volume, low-value supplier disbursements and marketplace payouts, but the primary corporate treasury, escrow of the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital, and FX hedging margin must sit with a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank. Contractually, the EMI agreement must be reviewed to ensure no rehypothecation, clear segregation of client funds, and EU e-money license (or equivalent) where the EMI is passporting into Switzerland; cross-border passported EMIs may only provide payment services to Swiss corporates without soliciting deposits if they act through a Swiss domestic bank as settlement agent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted for a Swiss AG of standard low-risk e-commerce profile, but in practice all Tier-1 Swiss banks (UBS, ZKB) require at least one in-person or live video-verified interview with each director and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) before account activation. There is no absolute statutory mandate for physical presence, but AMLA (Art. 3 and FINMA Circular 2016/07) requires the bank to establish UBO identity with 'due diligence adequate to the risk'; for non-resident or non-EU resident directors, banks almost invariably demand physical appearance at a Swiss branch or trusted foreign correspondent for signature verification. Practical recommendation: the Swiss managing director (if resident) appears physically at the ZKB or UBS branch in Zurich/Zug; non-resident directors execute a notarised and apostilled board resolution plus certified passport copies, and may be invited to a remote video identity verification using the bank's approved tooling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity or nominee shareholder structure where the ultimate owner is not transparent (e.g., layered holding across multiple jurisdictions)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss commercial register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) showing registered share ledger; signed UBO declaration per Art. 4 AMLA and Art. 51 ff. of the Ordinance on the Prevention of Money Laundering; corporate chart of ownership with percentages and tax IDs of each intermediate entity; notarised board resolution identifying the economic owner; audited annual financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a jurisdiction classified as high-risk by FATF/GAFI or a non-cooperative tax jurisdiction (e.g., source of share capital in a crypto-asset origin from Zug 'Crypto Valley' exchanges)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth file: brokerage statements, token custody wallet history, prior tax returns and Swiss stamp duty/tax clearance, signed confirmations of no criminal proceeds, exchange KYC evidence, and CHF-denominated bank transfer trail from a regulated institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value cross-border e-commerce receipts causing fragmented transaction flow anomalies (Klarna BNPL chargebacks, refunds, and rapid ticket velocity)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: E-commerce platform settlement reports (Shopify Payments ledger, Klarna reconciliation exports), 12-month projected transaction modelling, card network MCC/category code confirmation (MCC 5651 for apparel retail), refund and chargeback policy documentation, PCI-DSS compliance attestation, and contract evidence with marketplace payment servicers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/screening hits on counterparties, logistics providers, or payment beneficiaries domiciled in sanctioned or embargoed territories in the apparel supply chain (e.g., sourcing from restricted textile mills)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions and PEP screening logs (OFAC, SECO, EU, UN), full supplier vetting file with LEI numbers, contractual wrap with export-control and anti-boycott clauses, periodic negative-news monitoring reports, and a remediation protocol letter to the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between stated business revenue and banking volumes in the first year given the low minimum capital (CHF 100,000) of an AG relative to expected e-commerce throughput
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business cash-flow forecast, customer agreements with PSPs, marketing channel cost evidence, third-party e-commerce analytics, VAT/input-tax returns confirming sales, and audited projections prepared by a Swiss fiduciary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: shareholder equity or shareholder loan via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent to the Swiss AG's operating account at UBS/ZKB. Mandatory reference fields include the no. 70 purpose code: use 'Equity injection - formation of Swiss AG' (SNB statistical classification code 2301 – establishment of companies and participation in such companies) or for loans use code 2302/2801 (intercompany financial loans). Verify the same-day SWIFT confirmation and provide the bank with an executed capital payment confirmation board resolution. The wire must be denominated in CHF, EUR, or USD with the bank's FX conversion noted; ensure the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital is booked to the separate capital escrow account (Einzahlungskonto/Aktienkapitalkonto) until registration, then released to operating account. For subsequent recapitalisation via debt push-down, prepare a written intercompany loan agreement with arm's-length interest (safe-harbour per OECD TP guidance), Swiss withholding tax analysis if interest exceeds deductibility thresholds, and notify the SNB in the monthly balance-of-payments survey.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for supplier settlements in EUR, USD, CNY, CHF; SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for Euro-zone suppliers under EUR 100,000 per transaction. For large apparel procurements exceeding USD 500,000 or where the supplier requires bank risk, use an Irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600) issued by UBS/ZKB with MT700 dispatch and documents against payment (D/P) via documentary collection (MT400). Optional use of MT202 COV for forwarding interbank credits when supplier and bank differ. To support Klarna/BNPL receivables settlement, set up a merchant settlement account with an acquiring bank connected to the card networks (Visa/Mastercard/SIX Payment Services) and ensure funds are swept daily to the domestic Swiss concentration account. For FX payment conversion, use the bank's standard spot trade (T+2) or an automated currency sweep with a pre-agreed pip spread; avoid HKD/CNY cash-pooling without a licensed NDF if the supplier's currency is non-convertible.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (CHF/EUR, CHF/USD, CHF/GBP) - standard, freely permitted, documented under ISDA or Swiss Master Agreement; no SNB authorisation required for non-financial end-users
FX Swaps (roll-over/swap FX forwards) - permitted for treasury liquidity management

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for medium-term alignment of USD/EUR revenue with CHF operating costs and dividend repatriation - allowed with Swiss bank counterparty under EMIR reporting if above volume thresholds
Call and Put FX Options - permissible (European-style) for flexible hedging

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) - permissible exclusively for illiquid emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY offshore variant, INR); rarely required for CHF due to full convertibility; must be executed with a regulated bank and reported in financial statements as derivative instruments
Interest Rate/Currency Swaps with embedded FX for financing of cross-border inventory acquisition - permissible but subject to board derivative policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss Federal, Cantonal and Communal Corporate Income Tax Return (Steuererklärung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration at the registered office; duplicate data to Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due generally by 30 June for a 31 December balance sheet; extension to 30 September available upon written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4% p.a. on any extra tax; administrative penalty up to 30% of assessed tax where willful; reminders and enforced collection; persistent failure can initiate commercial register dissolution and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly Value Added Tax Return under Swiss VAT law (MWST/VAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each quarter-end (31 March, 30 June, 30 September, 31 December); annual reconciliation integrated in fourth-quarter return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes reminder fee (approx. CHF 40 per reminder); delay penalties up to 10% of the VAT due per tax period; severe or repeated delays may require VAT guarantee and entry in debt collection enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employer Wage Declaration for Old-Age, Survivors' and Invalidity Insurance (AHV/IV/EO/ALV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent AHV Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) for the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be submitted by 31 January of the year following the payroll year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Summary penalty proceedings up to CHF 30,000 per violation; contribution arrears plus default interest; criminal administrative complaint for repeated omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Notification of Bearer Share Information (Meldung über Inhaberaktien) — due only where bearer shares have been issued
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt) at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end (i.e., by 30 June for a 31 December balance-sheet date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Coercive fines by the commercial register (CHF 100 to 1,000 per violation); directors’ personal liability; repeated non-compliance may lead to ex officio strike-off from the commercial register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full ordinary audit is mandatory if the AG is listed, has bearer shares, or exceeds any two of these thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets CHF 20 million, net turnover CHF 40 million, 250 full-time employees on annual average. All other AGs require a limited audit unless eligible for full opt-out (fewer than 10 average full-time employees and consent of all shareholders).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP per Code of Obligations (Art. 958 et seq.); IFRS is a permitted alternative for consolidated or listed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not impose a dedicated annual UBO filing for private AGs. The board must maintain an accurate register of registered shareholders (Aktienbuch) and identify natural-person beneficial owners for AML/CRS purposes. All be sting share transfers are recorded immediately in the share register; bearer-issuing companies must annually state the total number and nominal amount of bearer shares to the commercial register within six months of the balance sheet date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers / Nominee Holdings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,200 – 6,500 for limited audit; USD 6,000 – 17,000 for ordinary audit
